metadata.title: fix(ui): admin UI "Show" toggle for gateway tokens, passwords, and header values
metadata.author: crivetimihai

description: > **Note:** This PR was re-created from #2980 due to repository maintenance. Your code and branch are intact. @omorros please verify everything looks good. ## Related Issue Closes #2968 --- ## Summary The `masked()` method in `GatewayRead` was unconditionally setting all `_unmasked` fields to `None`, which broke the admin UI "Show" toggle for gateway tokens, passwords, and header values. This adds an opt-in `preserve_unmasked` parameter so the permission-gated admin endpoint can receive the real values while all other callers remain unaffected. --- ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix --- ## Verification | Check | Command | Status | |---------------------------|-----------------|--------| | Unit tests (admin) | `pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_admin.py` | 775/775 passed | | Unit tests (schemas) | `pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/test_schemas.py` | 65/65 passed | | Doctests (gateway service)| `pytest --doctest-modules mcpgateway/services/gateway_service.py` | 25/25 passed | | Manual test | Admin UI "Show" toggle | Working | --- ## Checklist - [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`) - [ ] Tests added/updated for changes - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] No secrets or credentials committed --- ### Manual verification

reviews.author: jonpspri
reviews.body:
## Review Summary

Clean, minimal fix that correctly restores the admin UI "Show" toggle for gateway credentials while maintaining security for all other callers.

### Security

- `masked()` defaults to `preserve_unmasked=False` — safe by default.
- The only caller opting in is `admin_get_gateway`, which is protected by `AdminAuthMiddleware` (admin-only at middleware layer) and `@require_permission("gateways.read", allow_admin_bypass=False)`.
- Non-admin `get_gateway` in `main.py` and the vault plugin caller do not pass the flag — credentials remain fully masked.
- `preserve_unmasked` is keyword-only (`*`), preventing accidental positional misuse.

### Correctness

The `include_unmasked` flag threads cleanly from the admin route through the service layer to `masked()`. All existing call sites are unaffected.

### Test Coverage

Three new tests cover the critical paths:
- **Admin allow-path**: verifies `include_unmasked=True` is passed
- **Non-admin deny-path**: verifies the flag is NOT passed from the public route
- **Schema-level**: verifies `preserve_unmasked=True` preserves basic, bearer, and authheaders credentials

Existing `test_masked_auth_bearer_token_credentials` already covers the default (flag absent → `_unmasked` fields are `None`).

### Linting

All ruff warnings in changed files are pre-existing — no new issues introduced.

### Note

`admin_list_gateways` does not pass the flag, so the "Show" toggle in the list view may still not work. This is consistent with the scoped approach and the follow-up in #3346.

LGTM

commits.message:
fix: add test coverage for preserve_unmasked credential reveal (#3201)

Closes the differential coverage gap for the preserve_unmasked parameter
introduced in PR #3201. Adds tests verifying that masked(preserve_unmasked=True)
retains _unmasked fields for basic, bearer, and authheaders auth types, and that
admin_get_gateway passes include_unmasked=True to the gateway service.

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
commits.author: Jonathan Springer

fix(test): add deny-path test for non-admin gateway credential masking (#3201)

Assert that the non-admin GET /gateways/{id} route does not pass
include_unmasked, ensuring credentials stay masked outside the admin UI.
